title: Laser Engravers for Beginners: Diode Lasers Explained
metaDescription: What a diode laser engraver can and cannot do, and how four beginner models compare: LONGER RAY5 5W and 10W, SCULPFUN S9 and the SCULPFUN C1 mini.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: A diode laser engraver is the entry point to laser work: a compact machine that burns or marks wood, leather, cardboard, painted metal and similar materials by moving a focused laser beam over them. For a beginner the confusing part is the spec sheet: watts, spot size, working area, speed. This guide explains those terms in plain language and compares four catalog models that cover the range from a pocket-size mini to a 400 mm hobby machine, priced from $120.30 to $329.99.

items.label: Laser power (W)
items.value: Higher power cuts thicker material and engraves faster, but raises cost and safety needs. Compare the stated power of each listing, not marketing names.

items.label: Spot size (mm)
items.value: The size of the focused beam. A smaller spot gives finer detail: the C1 lists 0.04 mm, the S9 and RAY5 10W 0.06 mm, the RAY5 5W 0.08x0.08 mm.

items.label: Working area
items.value: The largest piece you can engrave without moving it: 150x130 mm (C1), 410x420 mm (S9), 400x400 mm (RAY5).

items.label: Speed (mm/min)
items.value: The RAY5 lists up to 24,000 mm/min, the C1 10,000 mm/min. Speed matters for big fills, less for small logos.

items.label: Connectivity
items.value: The RAY5 lists WiFi, a 3.5-inch touch screen and offline carving, so you can run jobs without a computer attached.

sections.title: The Four Models at a Glance

items.label: SCULPFUN C1 3W ($120.30)
items.value: Mini engraver, 150x130 mm area, 0.04 mm spot, 10,000 mm/min

items.label: SCULPFUN S9 5.5W ($198.64)
items.value: 410x420 mm area, 0.06 mm compressed spot, fixed focus, listing states it cuts 15 mm wood and 10 mm acrylic

items.label: LONGER RAY5 5W ($252.73)
items.value: 32-bit chipset, WiFi, 3.5" touch screen, offline carving, 400x400 mm, 0.08x0.08 mm spot

items.label: LONGER RAY5 10W ($329.99)
items.value: Same platform as the 5W with 10W power and a 0.06x0.06 mm spot

pros: The C1 is the cheapest way in at $120.30 and its 0.04 mm spot is the finest listed here, suited to small marks and detail
The S9 offers the largest area (410x420 mm) for the price, and its listing states 15 mm wood and 10 mm acrylic cutting
The RAY5 adds WiFi, a touch screen and offline carving, which removes the need to keep a laptop connected
The RAY5 10W costs about $77 more than the 5W and doubles the stated power, a clear upgrade path on the same machine
All four are diode lasers, so they work with common free and paid engraving software
cons: Diode lasers are best on organic and painted materials; do not expect to engrave bare metal or cut thick material quickly
The C1's 150x130 mm area limits project size
The S9 is fixed-focus, so you set height by hand, and the listing gives a power rating that is lower than the 10W class
Higher-power lasers need eye protection, ventilation and a safe workspace; budget for goggles and an extraction solution
Stated cutting capacity depends on the material and number of passes, so treat the listing numbers as best case

items.question: Which laser engraver should a first-time buyer pick?
items.answer: For small projects such as keychains, coasters and marking, the SCULPFUN C1 is the cheapest start. For a bigger bed and cutting thin wood or acrylic, the S9 is the value pick. If you want WiFi and offline use, choose the LONGER RAY5, and the 10W if you plan to cut rather than just engrave.

items.question: Is 5W or 10W enough?
items.answer: For engraving, 5W is usually enough. For cutting, more power means fewer passes and thicker material. The 10W RAY5 is the safer choice if you expect to cut.

items.question: What materials can a diode laser work on?
items.answer: Typically wood, plywood, leather, cardboard, paper, dark acrylic and painted or coated metal. Always check the material before burning it, since some plastics release harmful fumes.

items.question: Do I need safety equipment?
items.answer: Yes. Use laser-rated eye protection, ventilate the room or use an extractor, and never leave a running machine unattended. Our upcoming accessories guide covers beds, rotary rollers and extractors.

sections.content: Start by deciding the size of your projects and whether you will cut or only engrave. The C1 suits small detail work, the S9 gives the most area for the money, and the RAY5 is the comfortable, connected choice, with the 10W the one to buy if cutting matters. Whichever you choose, budget for eye protection and ventilation.
